title: Refine autoscaler metric composition and safety horizon
creator: Aisha Rao
description: Goal: evolve the Dedicated autoscaling policy engine to use a composite target metric and introduce a safety horizon that prevents oscillation and meets throughput guarantees under bursty workloads. We must balance latency SLOs, throughput guarantees for reserved pools, and cost by preventing unnecessary scale-ups. This ticket scopes metric composition, candidate scaling algorithms, safety limits (min/max, surge buffers, cooldowns, error budgets), and rollout/observability requirements.
notes: 2026-02-15: Kickoff with runtime and infra. Agreed constraints: must be implementable without wholesale runtime changes; prefer config-first rollout via policy builder.

2026-02-20: Prototype metric vector defined: (1) sustained_token_rate_per_gpu (30s window), (2) p95_latency_ms (1m window), (3) queue_depth (instant), (4) error_rate (5m). Weighting will be configurable per pool.
2026-02-24: Simulation run on 7 historical traces (customer and synthetic spikes). Observed oscillation when using only token_rate and p95 — added cooldown and step-size limits mitigated flapping.

2026-03-02: Design review with PM/Design. Decided to support two scaling algorithms initially: predictive windowed-slope (lightweight forecast) and hybrid step-PID for quick reaction + steady-state correction. Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Autoscaler+Metric+Composition+Design
2026-03-05: Security reviewed config surface. No sensitive data exposure. Affirmed that KMS changes not required.

2026-03-10: Implemented policy compiler changes to accept 'metric_vector' and 'safety_horizon' fields. End-to-end tests added to autoscale-sim suite. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/421
acceptance_criteria: Policy compiler accepts 'metric_vector' with weights and thresholds and persists to policy store
Two algorithms available in runtime flags: predictive-window and hybrid-step-pid
Safety horizon implemented: min_replicas, max_replicas, surge_buffer_pct, cooldown_seconds, step_limit
No more than 2x replica oscillation observed on provided spike traces in autoscale-sim
Dashboard showing per-pool metric_vector and scaling decisions in Console; alerting when safety limits prevent required capacity
decisions: Use configurable metric_vector rather than hard-coded single metric to support diverse workloads (batch-like token-heavy vs chat-like latency-sensitive).
Default weights: token_rate_per_gpu: 0.5, p95_latency_ms: 0.3, queue_depth: 0.15, error_rate: 0.05. Weights are adjustable per pool and can be overridden by customers with Dedicated contracts.

Implement hybrid-step-pid as primary algorithm for GA: step-scaling to react to large, fast spikes, with a lightweight PID loop smoothing steady-state error. Predictive-window added as opt-in for pools with stable periodicity.
Introduce 'safety_horizon' concept: a sliding time window during which scale-downs are throttled and surge buffers are reserved to meet short SLO bursts. Default safety_horizon = 180s (configurable).
Cooldowns: 120s between scale-up events for step-scaling and 300s between scale-downs unless escalated by sustained low utilization.

Failure mode: if autoscaler cannot satisfy throughput_guarantee within safety limits, mark pool critical and trigger fallback routing to adjacent pool or model-variant that uses less GPU memory (documented fallback policy).
next_steps: Ship policy compiler change behind feature flag and create policy templates for standard pool types (chat-low-latency, batch-high-throughput).
Integrate metric_vector visualization into Console's per-pool dashboard; expose current composite score and per-metric contribution.
Run extended simulation across 30 customer traces and adjust default weights and safety_horizon if >1.5x oscillation seen.
Schedule canary rollout to non-critical pools for 2 weeks and monitor SLO and cost delta.
Follow-up ticket to add ML-based predictor (windowed-ARIMA/LSTM) as an experiment pending results.
